description:
About the Position

The Department of Physics at Stockholm University invites applications for a PhD student position in chemical physics, focused on quantum-chemical calculations of X-ray spectra in the condensed phase. The project develops and applies electronic-structure methods to predict and interpret X-ray spectroscopy of liquids, solutions and solid interfaces - connecting spectral signatures to molecular structure and dynamics. The position is a salaried four-year doctoral employment under the Swedish collective agreement.

X-ray spectroscopy is a primary tool for probing chemical states in real materials and environments, and Stockholm hosts leading activities in both the theory of X-ray processes and synchrotron-based experiments. The doctoral candidate will implement and run quantum-chemical calculations, compare results with experimental spectra, and contribute methods development, with opportunities to engage with measurement campaigns at international facilities such as MAX IV and DESY.

Candidate Profile

Applicants hold a master's degree in chemical physics, physical chemistry, physics or a related field, with a good grounding in quantum mechanics and computational work. Experience with electronic-structure software, spectroscopy or programming is an advantage. Applications run through the Varbi recruitment system with CV, transcripts, references and a statement of interests.

Highlights

  • PhD in chemical physics: quantum-chemical X-ray spectroscopy
  • Condensed-phase liquids, solutions and interfaces
  • Electronic-structure methods development and application
  • Links to synchrotron experiments (MAX IV, DESY)
  • Salaried four-year employment per Swedish collective agreement
  • Application via the Varbi recruitment system

About Stockholm University

Stockholm University is a public research university in the Swedish capital with roughly 30,000 students and a strong research profile in the natural sciences, psychology, humanities, law and social sciences. Many of its departments collaborate with national research institutes located on the same campus areas, including the neighbouring Science for Life Laboratory environment. Doctoral students in Sweden are employed on paid contracts with collective-agreement salaries and full social benefits. PhD and postdoctoral vacancies are recruited through the national Varbi system used by Swedish universities.
